record.title: Instrument-mounted demonstrations train an appendectomy policy tested in live rabbits
record.summary: A Sept. 22 preprint reports an end-to-end pipeline that records instrument pose and jaw state from sensors mounted on a surgeon’s ordinary laparoscopic tools, aligns the sensor channels against robot ground truth, and trains a bimanual policy without robot-collected demonstrations. After closed-loop simulator selection among 31 configurations, the authors retrained on 849 demonstrations from four live rabbits and tested on four additional rabbits; the policy completed appendectomy in three of four under shared autonomy with electrosurgery armed. A surgeon chose the surgical phase because the vision-based phase predictor failed under the deployment endoscope. This is a small animal study, not full autonomy or clinical evidence.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors describe an instrument-mounted logger using inertial, time-of-flight and Hall sensors to estimate tool state without an external camera or tracker, with per-channel latency matching against robot ground truth.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The policy trained from hand-held instrument demonstrations completed appendectomy in three of four additional live rabbits under shared autonomy with the surgeon selecting the surgical phase.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report training on 849 in-vivo demonstrations from four live rabbits and use of a policy configuration selected through 31 simulator configurations.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The study is limited to four deployment animals on one day; the surgeon selected surgical phase because the vision-based predictor agreed with the surgeon on only 24.6% of policy control steps under the deployment endoscope.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent animal replication or human clinical evaluation was inspected; current report uses four deployment animals.

brief.importance_rationale: If hand-held instrument sensing can repeatedly supply usable training demonstrations for robotic surgery, it could open a broader data source and alter surgical-policy development. The score reflects the potential pipeline consequence, not the small four-animal outcome or readiness for clinical use.
limitations: Author-reported, not independently reproduced in this activation.
The deployment set contains four live rabbits; the policy completed the task in three.
This was shared autonomy: a surgeon selected the phase because the vision-based phase predictor performed poorly under the deployment endoscope.
No human-patient or clinical safety evidence is reported.
The robot provides calibration ground truth and executes the policy, even though it did not collect training demonstrations.
brief.summary: A Sept. 22 preprint reports an end-to-end pipeline that records instrument pose and jaw state from sensors mounted on a surgeon’s ordinary laparoscopic tools, aligns the sensor channels against robot ground truth, and trains a bimanual policy without robot-collected demonstrations. After closed-loop simulator selection among 31 configurations, the authors retrained on 849 demonstrations from four live rabbits and tested on four additional rabbits; the policy completed appendectomy in three of four under shared autonomy with electrosurgery armed. A surgeon chose the surgical phase because the vision-based phase predictor failed under the deployment endoscope. This is a small animal study, not full autonomy or clinical evidence.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report successful appendectomy completion in three of four additional live rabbits, with electrosurgery armed, after training on 849 hand-held in-vivo demonstrations; the surgeon manually supplied procedure phase.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint describes an end-to-end sensing and training pipeline. It reports 3/4 appendectomy completions on additional live rabbits under shared autonomy; no independent result was established here.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype and two demonstration corpora are described as released by the paper authors; code/data were not independently run here.
technical.mechanism: A compact instrument-mounted logger combines IMU orientation, time-of-flight insertion depth and Hall-sensor jaw state. Per-channel latencies are aligned to robot ground truth before forming observation/action pairs. A diffusion policy with DINOv3 is selected using simulator closed-loop rollouts, then retrained on in-vivo demonstrations.
technical.regime: Bimanual laparoscopic appendectomy using two FR3 arms and standard instruments. Four live rabbits supplied demonstrations and four additional rabbits were deployment subjects; each deployment animal had one run. The study was submitted to ICRA 2027.
technical.reproducibility: Paper reports simulator and in-vivo protocol details and links data corpora. Independent replication, additional-animal testing and clinical translation are open.
technical.strongest_baseline: In simulator ablations, selected DINOv3 policy with one unfrozen block reached 81% full-approach completion versus 12% for ResNet-18 and 44% with frozen DINOv3; these are simulator configuration comparisons, not an independent baseline for live-animal completion.

brief.title: Instrument-mounted demonstrations train an appendectomy policy tested in live rabbits
brief.why_it_matters: If the pipeline generalizes, it could turn otherwise discarded motion from hand-held minimally invasive surgery into policy-training data and reduce dependence on robot-specific demonstrations. The current result is an early in-vivo animal demonstration with explicit human phase control, not evidence of patient safety or autonomous surgery.
